formulaBlock.normalization: Packet canonicalInci used as normalized list (ID-2); positions are one-based on that list.

cleansingStrength.rationale: C1 with a reinforcing route: SLES (2) defining plus prominent Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (3) -> strong, despite the betaine buffer (6).

conditioningLevel.rationale: C2 met: early silicone (Dimethiconol 10, prominent; Dimethicone 13 supporting), cationic polymer (Guar HPTC 15), pearlizing route (Glycol Distearate 7) and a closed-list humectant (Panthenol 24) -> multiple complementary systems -> high, even in a strong chassis.
conditioningLevel.counterSignal: Guar and Panthenol are late (15, 24) and the humectant element is trace; strong double-anionic cleansing.

weightPotential.rationale: Silicone system (Dimethiconol 10, Dimethicone 13) with cationic guar (15) is a plausible deposition system; strong reset limits accumulation -> moderate. Not the W1 set (no amodimethicone), so the full method decides.
weightPotential.counterSignal: Two silicones plus a guar coacervate are designed to deposit; strong reset argues lighter.

depositionLoad.rationale: Two silicones (10, 13) plus cationic guar (15); no lipid, protein or film former.

persistence.rationale: Silicone deposited via guar coacervate is moderately persistent.

resetCapacity.rationale: C1 reinforced: SLES + SLS (+ late TEA-DDBS).

weightPotential.whyThisBand: One meaningfully persistent silicone/cationic deposition system, offset by strong reset.
weightPotential.whyNotNeighborBand: Not high: no W-RICH (no prominent payload lipid), no second cationic or film former, and reset is strong. Not low: two distinct families (silicone + cationic polymer) form a deliberate deposition system; strong reset does not face only light routes (W2).
weightPotential.limitingFactor: Silicone/guar levels unknown; reset vs. deposition balance.

careDirection.note: Silicone/guar conditioning is generic; no humectant cluster (Panthenol 24 trace) and no protein/damage cluster.
